models.name: political_forum_post_states
models.description: Defines all possible states a post can have in its lifecycle. Used as reference by political_forum_posts to indicate current status. States include: draft, published, moderation_queue, deleted, archived, restored. This table ensures consistency across the system by providing authoritative state definitions for post lifecycle management.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: The machine-readable name of the post state (e.g., 'draft', 'published'). Must be unique.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable description of what this state means in business context. Explains when this state is applied and what actions are allowed.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this state definition was created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this state definition was last modified. Should be rarely updated as these are reference data.

models.name: political_forum_moderation_status
models.description: Defines the possible moderation states for content. Used as reference by political_forum_posts and political_forum_comments to indicate verification status. States include: unverified, verified, flagged, under_review, rejected. This table defines the authoritative set of moderation statuses that can be applied to content, ensuring consistent behavior across the system.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: The machine-readable name of the moderation status (e.g., 'verified', 'flagged'). Must be unique.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable description of what this moderation status means in business context. Explains when this status is applied and its implications for content visibility.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this moderation status definition was created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this moderation status definition was last modified. Should be rarely updated as these are reference data.

models.name: political_forum_attachment_types
models.description: Defines the allowed file types for attachments to posts. Used as reference by political_forum_post_attachments to validate uploaded files. Types include: image (jpg, jpeg, png, gif), document (pdf, doc, docx, txt). This table ensures system-wide consistency in allowed attachment formats and provides metadata for UI display (e.g., icons for different file types).

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: The machine-readable name of the attachment type category (e.g., 'image', 'document'). Must be unique.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable description of this attachment type category and what file extensions it includes.

plainFields.name: file_extensions
plainFields.description: Comma-separated list of allowed file extensions for this attachment type (e.g., 'jpg,jpeg,png,gif'). Used for upload validation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this attachment type definition was created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this attachment type definition was last modified. Should be rarely updated as these are reference data.

models.name: political_forum_system_settings
models.description: Stores system-wide configuration parameters for the political discussion board. Used as reference by the backend to enforce business rules such as character limits, timeouts, and feature toggles. This table contains vital parameters that control system behavior without requiring code deployment to change.

plainFields.name: setting_key
plainFields.description: Unique identifier for this system setting (e.g., 'MAX_POST_LENGTH', 'EDIT_WINDOW_HOURS'). Must be unique.

plainFields.name: setting_value
plainFields.description: The value of this system setting. Stored as string to accommodate various data types (integers, booleans, strings) that can be parsed by the application layer.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable description of what this setting controls, how it affects the system, and its business purpose.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this system setting was created or first registered.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this system setting was last modified.

models.name: political_forum_citizens
models.description: Primary actor table storing citizen user identity and authentication data. Citizens create posts, comment, and attach files. Their data is linked to all actions performed by them, including posts and reports. Managed through registration and login workflows. {@link political_forum_citizen_sessions.id}

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address for citizen communication and login. Must be verified.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password for authentication. Never stored in plaintext. Required for login.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: User-chosen display name for public visibility in posts/comments. Can be changed.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the citizen account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the citizen account was last updated (e.g. display name change).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-delete timestamp. If null, account is active. If set, account is marked for deletion.

plainFields.name: email_verified
plainFields.description: Flag indicating whether the citizen's email has been verified via email link.

models.name: political_forum_citizen_sessions
models.description: Session records for authenticated citizens. Each session is tied to a unique citizen and tracks the login context. Used for access control and revocation. Follows strict session pattern: no token storage, no updated_at, no deleted_at. {@link political_forum_citizens.id}

foreignFields.name: political_forum_citizen_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the citizen this session belongs to. {@link political_forum_citizens.id}

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address used during this session login.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL of the page where the session was initiated.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL that led the user to the login page.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created on login.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session expires or was manually invalidated. If null, session is still active.

models.name: political_forum_moderators
models.description: Primary actor table storing moderator identity and authentication data. Moderators have elevated permissions to delete, lock, and verify content. Their actions are logged for audit. Managed by system administrators only. {@link political_forum_moderator_sessions.id}

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address for moderator communication and login. Must be verified.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password for authentication. Never stored in plaintext. Required for login.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: User-chosen display name for public visibility in moderation logs.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderator account was created by system administrator.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderator account was last updated (e.g. display name change).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-delete timestamp. If null, account is active. If set, account is marked for deletion.

plainFields.name: email_verified
plainFields.description: Flag indicating whether the moderator's email has been verified via email link.

models.name: political_forum_moderator_sessions
models.description: Session records for authenticated moderators. Each session is tied to a unique moderator and tracks login context. Used for access control and audit trails. Follows strict session pattern: no token storage, no updated_at, no deleted_at. {@link political_forum_moderators.id}

foreignFields.name: political_forum_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the moderator this session belongs to. {@link political_forum_moderators.id}

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address used during this session login.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL of the page where the session was initiated.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL that led the user to the login page.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created on login.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session expires or was manually invalidated. If null, session is still active.

models.name: political_forum_posts
models.description: Main entity representing citizen-submitted political discussion posts. Posts are primary content objects with a lifecycle: created, published, edited (within 24h), locked, or deleted. This table stores raw content and metadata. Relationships: references political_forum_citizens (author), political_forum_post_states (status), and political_forum_post_attachments (via join).

foreignFields.name: citizen_id
foreignFields.description: Author's citizen account. {@link political_forum_citizens.id}.

foreignFields.name: post_state_id
foreignFields.description: Current state of the post (e.g., published, pending, deleted, locked). {@link political_forum_post_states.id}.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Title of the post. Required field with 3-150 characters as per requirements.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Main content body of the post. Must be 10-5000 characters as per business rules.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the post was created. Always non-null.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the post was last edited. Updated only if edited within 24-hour window.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the post was deleted by a moderator. Null if not deleted. Required for soft delete audit.

plainFields.name: edit_count
plainFields.description: Number of times this post has been edited within the 24-hour window. Used for audit and transparency.

models.name: political_forum_comments
models.description: Public comments made by citizens on posts. Comments are independent entities with their own lifecycle and moderation status. They are not subsidiary to posts because they require independent search (e.g., all comments by user X), moderation, and tracking. Associated with a post via foreign key but managed as primary entity.

foreignFields.name: post_id
foreignFields.description: Parent post this comment replies to. {@link political_forum_posts.id}.

foreignFields.name: citizen_id
foreignFields.description: Author's citizen account. {@link political_forum_citizens.id}.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Content of the comment. Must be 5-1500 characters as per requirements.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was posted. Always non-null.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was last edited (within 24h of posting).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was deleted by a moderator. Null if not deleted. Required for soft delete audit.

models.name: political_forum_post_attachments
models.description: Stores metadata for files uploaded with political forum posts. Each record represents one attachment linked to a specific post. Attachments are managed solely through the post they belong to — no independent user actions on attachments. No comment attachments allowed. File types are restricted to images (JPG, PNG, GIF) and documents (PDF, TXT) as per business rules. File size capped at 10MB per file. Fields include original filename, cloud storage path, size in bytes, upload timestamp, and deletion state. When a post is deleted, attachments are preserved for 13 months for audit, then purged. This table follows the subsidiary stance — attachments are never independently created or managed. Their visibility and lifecycle are entirely dependent on the parent post's state. {@link political_forum_posts} is the parent. {@link political_forum_attachment_types} defines the allowed MIME type categories.

foreignFields.name: political_forum_post_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the post this attachment belongs to. {@link political_forum_posts.id}

foreignFields.name: political_forum_attachment_type_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the allowed file type category (e.g., image/jpeg, application/pdf). {@link political_forum_attachment_types.id}

plainFields.name: original_filename
plainFields.description: The original filename provided by the user during upload. Preserved exactly as submitted for display and audit purposes. Used for user-facing display and full-text search.

plainFields.name: file_path
plainFields.description: The external URL pointing to the file stored in cloud storage. Generated and returned by cloud service upon upload. Used to render file previews or download links. Never stored locally.

plainFields.name: file_size
plainFields.description: Size of the uploaded file in bytes. Must be <= 10,485,760 (10MB). Enforced during upload. Used for budgeting storage and compliance with attachment rules.

plainFields.name: uploaded_at
plainFields.description: The precise timestamp when the file was successfully uploaded to cloud storage. Different from created_at to reflect actual cloud ingestion time, not system record creation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this attachment record was created in the database.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this attachment record was last updated (e.g., renamed metadata, status change).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete flag. When null, attachment is active. When set, the attachment is marked for deletion but retained for audit (13 months). After 13 months, the file is purged from cloud storage. Indicates permanent deletion via user or moderator action on the parent post.

models.name: political_forum_moderation_actions
models.description: Audit log of moderator actions: deletion, locking, or verification of posts. Each record represents a single action taken by a moderator on a post. Records are immutable and used exclusively for audit, accountability, and transparency. Tracks who did what, when, and why. Links to political_forum_moderators.id and political_forum_posts.id.

foreignFields.name: political_forum_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: The moderator who performed this action. {@link political_forum_moderators.id}.

foreignFields.name: political_forum_post_id
foreignFields.description: The post that was affected by this action. {@link political_forum_posts.id}.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of moderator action: 'delete', 'lock', or 'verify'. Case-sensitive string that defines the nature of the moderation event.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Brief description provided by the moderator explaining why this action was taken. Required for accountability and to inform the post author in notifications.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderation action was executed. Immutable audit record. This field establishes chronological order of events.

models.name: political_forum_post_modifications
models.description: Track the historical state changes of posts due to moderation actions. Records each instance when a post's public status changed to 'deleted', 'locked', or 'verified'. This table captures the result state of a post at time of action, while political_forum_moderation_actions captures the action itself. Immutable audit record. Links to political_forum_posts.id and political_forum_moderation_actions.id.

foreignFields.name: political_forum_post_id
foreignFields.description: The post whose state was modified. {@link political_forum_posts.id}.

foreignFields.name: political_forum_moderation_action_id
foreignFields.description: The moderation action that caused this state change. {@link political_forum_moderation_actions.id}.

plainFields.name: new_state
plainFields.description: The target state applied to the post: 'deleted', 'locked', or 'verified'. Used by frontend to display banners, badges, or removed notices.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the post's state was changed. This field correlates with political_forum_moderation_actions.created_at for full audit trail alignment.

models.name: political_forum_post_reports
models.description: Records reports submitted by citizens against specific political forum posts. Each report captures the reporting citizen, the post being reported, the reason for the report, and its current moderation status. This table is independent and allows moderators to efficiently review and filter all reported posts across the system without needing to load the parent post content. Each report can be independently queried, sorted, and archived. Linked to political_forum_posts.id and political_forum_citizens.id.

foreignFields.name: political_forum_post_id
foreignFields.description: The post being reported. {@link political_forum_posts.id}

foreignFields.name: political_forum_citizen_id
foreignFields.description: The citizen who submitted the report. {@link political_forum_citizens.id}

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Status of the report. Values: pending, reviewed, dismissed, escalated.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The reason or explanation provided by the citizen for why they are reporting this post. Should contain at least 10 characters.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of when the report was submitted.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to the report status or reason.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. If null, the report is active.

models.name: political_forum_comment_reports
models.description: Records reports submitted by citizens against specific political forum comments. Each report captures the reporting citizen, the comment being reported, the reason for the report, and its current moderation status. This table is independent and allows moderators to efficiently review and filter all reported comments across the system regardless of the parent post. Each report can be independently queried, sorted, and archived. Linked to political_forum_comments.id and political_forum_citizens.id.

foreignFields.name: political_forum_comment_id
foreignFields.description: The comment being reported. {@link political_forum_comments.id}

foreignFields.name: political_forum_citizen_id
foreignFields.description: The citizen who submitted the report. {@link political_forum_citizens.id}

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Status of the report. Values: pending, reviewed, dismissed, escalated.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The reason or explanation provided by the citizen for why they are reporting this comment. Should contain at least 10 characters.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of when the report was submitted.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to the report status or reason.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. If null, the report is active.

models.name: political_forum_system_parameters
models.description:
Global system configuration parameters that control the behavior of the political forum. This table defines system-wide limits and policies that apply uniformly to all citizens and moderators. Values in this table are managed through administrative interfaces, not directly by end users. These settings provide the foundation for business rules such as edit windows, file size restrictions, and permitted attachment types.

This table is referenced by all components of the system to enforce consistent behavior. It is updated rarely through secure administrative channels and does not require user-facing CRUD operations.

All values are authoritative and override any default hard-coded values in the application layer.

For example:
- edit_window_hours determines how long citizens can edit their own posts (24 hours)
- max_file_size_mb sets the maximum upload size per file (10 MB)
- allowed_attachment_types defines which MIME types are acceptable for uploads

This entity has no relationships to other tables - it is a singleton configuration store.

See also: {@link political_forum_audit_logs} for change history of these settings.

plainFields.name: edit_window_hours
plainFields.description: The number of hours during which a citizen may edit their own post after initial submission. Standard value is 24 hours.

plainFields.name: max_file_size_mb
plainFields.description: Maximum size allowed for any single attachment file uploaded with a post, in megabytes. Standard value is 10 MB.

plainFields.name: allowed_attachment_types
plainFields.description: Comma-separated list of allowed file extensions for attachments. Includes image types (.jpg, .jpeg, .png, .gif) and document types (.pdf, .txt, .doc, .docx). Must be stored as a single string for simplicity in application logic.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this system configuration record was created. Immutable after creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this system configuration record was last updated. Updated automatically on every change.

models.name: political_forum_system_parameters_current
models.description:
Current system-wide configuration parameters that control the behavior of the political forum. This table defines a single authoritative set of system-wide limits and policies that apply uniformly to all citizens and moderators. Values in this table are managed through administrative interfaces, not directly by end users. These settings provide the foundation for business rules such as edit windows, file size restrictions, and permitted attachment types.

This table is referenced by all components of the system to enforce consistent behavior. It is updated rarely through secure administrative channels and does not require user-facing CRUD operations.

This current value reference is always the latest commit of configuration in the system.

See also: {@link political_forum_system_parameter_snapshots} for historical versions.

See also: {@link political_forum_audit_logs} for change history of these settings.

foreignFields.name: moderator_id
foreignFields.description: The moderator who last modified this configuration. References {@link political_forum_moderators.id}.

plainFields.name: edit_window_hours
plainFields.description: The number of hours during which a citizen may edit their own post after initial submission. Standard value is 24 hours.

plainFields.name: max_file_size_mb
plainFields.description: Maximum size allowed for any single attachment file uploaded with a post, in megabytes. Standard value is 10 MB.

plainFields.name: allowed_attachment_types
plainFields.description: Comma-separated list of allowed file extensions for attachments. Includes image types (.jpg, .jpeg, .png, .gif) and document types (.pdf, .txt, .doc, .docx). Must be stored as a single string for simplicity in application logic.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this system configuration record was created. Immutable after creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this system configuration record was last updated. Updated automatically on every change.

plainFields.name: updated_by
plainFields.description: The moderator ID who last modified this configuration. References {@link political_forum_moderators.id}.

models.name: political_forum_system_parameter_snapshots
models.description:
Historical snapshots of system-wide configuration parameters. This table captures point-in-time versions of the political_forum_system_parameters_current table for audit trail, compliance, and forensic analysis.

Each record represents a configuration state and is immutable. Whenever the current configuration is updated, a new snapshot is created instead of modifying existing records.

This enables:
- Full audit trail of system policy changes
- Compliance with regulatory requirements (GDPR, HIPAA if applicable)
- Forensic investigations into configuration-related incidents
- Rollback capability to previous configuration states if needed

This table is write-once and read-only from any external interface.

See also: {@link political_forum_system_parameters_current} for the current configuration value.

See also: {@link political_forum_audit_logs} for system-level audit trail of what changed.

foreignFields.name: political_forum_system_parameters_current_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the current configuration state that was snapshotted. References {@link political_forum_system_parameters_current.id}.

foreignFields.name: moderator_id
foreignFields.description: The moderator who performed the configuration change being snapped. References {@link political_forum_moderators.id}.

plainFields.name: edit_window_hours
plainFields.description: The number of hours during which a citizen may edit their own post after initial submission. Standard value is 24 hours. This value is captured at time of snapshot.

plainFields.name: max_file_size_mb
plainFields.description: Maximum size allowed for any single attachment file uploaded with a post, in megabytes. Standard value is 10 MB. This value is captured at time of snapshot.

plainFields.name: allowed_attachment_types
plainFields.description: Comma-separated list of allowed file extensions for attachments. Includes image types (.jpg, .jpeg, .png, .gif) and document types (.pdf, .txt, .doc, .docx). Must be stored as a single string for simplicity in application logic. This value is captured at time of snapshot.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this exact configuration snapshot was generated. This is NOT the same as when the current configuration was last updated - this is when the snapshot was created.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable description of what changed in this configuration update. e.g., 'Increased file size limit from 5MB to 10MB due to user feedback','Reduced edit window from 48 to 24 hours','Added .mp4 extension to allowed types'

models.name: political_forum_audit_logs
models.description:
Immutable audit log entries that record all significant system events for compliance and forensic purposes. This is the main entity that coordinates the polymorphic actor and target systems using IDs and discriminators. Uses actor_log_id and entity_log_id to reference specific subtype tables based on actor_type and target_type.

All direct foreign keys have been removed and replaced with discriminator + subtype pattern to preserve referential integrity and normalization. Every audit entry is validated against the subtype relationships rather than direct database FKs.

Links to political_forum_audit_log_of_citizens, political_forum_audit_log_of_moderators, political_forum_audit_log_targets through their respective ID fields. Dependent entirely on subtype tables to resolve actor and target identity with type safety.

foreignFields.name: actor_log_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key to either political_forum_audit_log_of_citizens.id or political_forum_audit_log_of_moderators.id, determined by actor_type. This ensures referential integrity while enabling polymorphic actor tracking. Never references directly to citizens or moderators.

foreignFields.name: entity_log_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key to political_forum_audit_log_targets.id. This point of reference resolves the target_type and enables JOIN to one of the specific target subtypes (post, comment, session).

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Specifies the type of actor performing the action. Must be exactly "citizen" or "moderator" as defined in the authentication system. Used with actor_log_id to determine which subtype table to join.

plainFields.name: target_type
plainFields.description: Specifies the type of entity being audited. Must be one of: "post", "comment", "session". Used with entity_log_id to determine which target subtype to join during query resolution.

plainFields.name: action
plainFields.description: Type of action taken. Valid values: "created", "modified", "deleted", "locked", "verified", "login", "logout", "report", "flagged". Derived from business rules governing system events.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: A human-readable description of the action performed, including optional reason provided by moderator (e.g., "Removed for hate speech") or system context (e.g., "Post flagged by 5 users"). Required for forensic accountability.

plainFields.name: old_state
plainFields.description: JSON string representing the state of the target entity before the action. For example: {"title": "Original Title", "text": "Original content"}. Use for change comparison and audit recovery.

plainFields.name: new_state
plainFields.description: JSON string representing the state of the target entity after the action. For example: {"title": "Updated Title", "text": "Updated content"}. Contains the final state after modification, deletion, or verification.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: The public IP address used by the actor when performing the action. Captured from HTTP request header for accountability.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: The HTTP User-Agent header sent by the client when performing the action. Used for identifying device or browser type for forensic analysis.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The precise UTC timestamp when the audit event was recorded by the system. Always uses server clock to ensure immutability. Follows ISO 8601 format.

models.name: political_forum_audit_log_of_citizens
models.description:
Subtype entity for audit logs executed specifically by citizens. This table enforces referential integrity by linking only to political_forum_citizens.id. The main political_forum_audit_logs table references this via actor_log_id, ensuring that all audit logs by citizens have a valid actor identity.

Does not require additional fields beyond the relationship to citizen. Cornerstone of polymorphic actor pattern.

foreignFields.name: political_forum_citizen_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the citizen who performed the audited action. Must be non-null and link directly to political_forum_citizens.id. Ensures valid actor authentication context.

models.name: political_forum_audit_log_of_moderators
models.description:
Subtype entity for audit logs executed specifically by moderators. This table enforces referential integrity by linking only to political_forum_moderators.id. The main political_forum_audit_logs table references this via actor_log_id, ensuring that all audit logs by moderators have a valid actor identity.

Does not require additional fields beyond the relationship to moderator. Cornerstone of polymorphic actor pattern.

foreignFields.name: political_forum_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the moderator who performed the audited action. Must be non-null and link directly to political_forum_moderators.id. Ensures valid actor authentication context.

models.name: political_forum_audit_log_target_of_posts
models.description:
Subtype entity for audit logs targeting political_forum_posts. Links the audit entry to the post being modified, deleted, locked, or verified. This ensures referential integrity for post-targeted events.

Does not require additional fields beyond the relationship to post. Cornerstone of polymorphic target pattern.

foreignFields.name: political_forum_post_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the post being audited. Must be non-null and link directly to political_forum_posts.id. Applies to actions: created, modified, deleted, locked, verified.

models.name: political_forum_audit_log_target_of_comments
models.description:
Subtype entity for audit logs targeting political_forum_comments. Links the audit entry to the comment being modified or deleted. This ensures referential integrity for comment-targeted events.

Does not require additional fields beyond the relationship to comment. Cornerstone of polymorphic target pattern.

foreignFields.name: political_forum_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the comment being audited. Must be non-null and link directly to political_forum_comments.id. Applies to actions: created, modified, deleted, flagged, reported.

models.name: political_forum_audit_log_target_of_sessions
models.description:
Subtype entity for audit logs targeting user sessions. Links the audit entry to the citizen_session being logged in or out. This ensures referential integrity for session-based audit events.

Does not require additional fields beyond the relationship to session. Cornerstone of polymorphic target pattern.

foreignFields.name: political_forum_citizen_session_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the citizen session being audited. Must be non-null and link directly to political_forum_citizen_sessions.id. Applies to actions: login, logout.

models.name: political_forum_audit_log_targets
models.description:
Main entity for audit log target types. Serves as the discriminator for different entities being audited.

Stores the target_type (post, comment, session) and links to respective subtype tables (political_forum_audit_log_target_of_posts, etc.). This allows the main audit_log table to reference exactly one target entity with full type safety and referential integrity.

Must be used with target_type field in political_forum_audit_logs to select the correct subtype for target resolution.

plainFields.name: target_type

models.name: political_forum_analytics_events
models.description: Event log for analytics tracking system-wide user and moderator actions. This table captures summaries of operational events (post creation, comment addition, moderation actions) to enable reporting without impacting transactional tables. Each entry represents a single event triggered by system activity. The actor is either a citizen or moderator, and the target is either a post or comment. This data is append-only and used exclusively for business intelligence. References to political_forum_posts, political_forum_comments, political_forum_citizens, and political_forum_moderators are maintained for audit and correlation.

foreignFields.name: target_post_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the target post if the event is related to a post. {@link political_forum_posts.id}

foreignFields.name: target_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the target comment if the event is related to a comment. {@link political_forum_comments.id}

foreignFields.name: actor_citizen_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the citizen who initiated the event, if applicable (e.g., post_created or comment_added). {@link political_forum_citizens.id}

foreignFields.name: actor_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the moderator who performed the action, if applicable (e.g., post_deleted or thread_locked). {@link political_forum_moderators.id}

plainFields.name: event_type

plainFields.name: context
plainFields.description: Optional contextual JSON string with additional event details (e.g., file count, reason for deletion, IP address).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the event was logged in the analytics system.

models.name: political_forum_archived_posts

This is a snapshot table, so it is not editable and only populated through system-triggered archival process. {@link political_forum_posts.id}
